name: Private Enterprise
description: Performance marketers buy US virtual phone numbers in bulk, then route, record, and attribute the calls, with texts on top. Billing is a prepaid wallet. The menu is 30 cents a number each month and 2 cents a minute. One person. The listing does not show a domain, so there is no homepage here.

mentions.evidence: $14,224 L30, updated 24 November 2026. All-time $96,333. The monthly line shows nothing, because customers pay from a prepaid wallet. The listing says it is growing 6 percent month over month, and it states a 75 percent margin. The founder says about $88,700 in the last 12 months, that October 2026 was 7.5 times October 2025, about 26 paying businesses, and about 2 hours a month to run. Launched June 2025. Still listed for sale at $325,000.
mentions.indieAngle: One person resells numbers and minutes and puts a dashboard on top. The listing says about 26 businesses are enough for the current cash.

whyItPrints: Lead-gen agencies need a number on the ad and a record of who called. They top up a wallet, and the work is light.
whyThisMatters:
The listing does not name a product and does not show a site. It sells US phone numbers to people who run pay-per-call ads. They buy numbers in bulk, route the call, record it, and see which ad it came from. Texts sit on top. One person. It launched in June 2025.

Customers pay from a prepaid wallet, so a monthly subscription line never fills in. The cash to look at is the last 30 days. Stripe is connected for that number. The founder says a couple of dozen businesses, no refunds in a year, and about two hours of work a month. On his telling, this October was several times last October. The business is up for sale.

The menu is a small charge for each number and a smaller charge for each minute. Those are prices. The margin on the listing is the gap between the carrier's wholesale rate and what the agency pays.
